messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Layperson summary for hosted API & console: subprocessors & cross-border transfers

Team —

I've pulled together a short "layperson" paragraph plus a two-bullet FAQ that we want to publish in the Console privacy panel and the hosted API docs. Goal: make subprocessors and cross-border transfers clearly understandable to product teams and procurement without legalese.

Draft attached: hosted-lay-summary_v1.docx. Also attached current subprocessor map for reference.

Asks:
- Kimberly: language sanity-check vs. DPA (do we accidentally promise something we can't?)
- Laura: sales-facing framing — will this answer the typical questions your reps hear?
- Vanessa: engineering copy constraints — any platform wording you need us to avoid?
- Stephanie: UX microcopy — readability and where to put the snippet in the Console.

I tried to avoid technical transfer terms like "EU SCCs" in the main blurb — kept them for the FAQ — but happy to adjust. Please reply with line edits or accept/reject. Deadlines: ACME legal has asked for an initial public-facing blurb by EOD Friday so they can include it in their procurement packet.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior PM, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Layperson summary for hosted API & console: subprocessors & cross-border transfers

Thanks Marcus — good work on the first pass. Quick notes inline and a couple of suggested alternate sentences below (I've pasted the lead paragraph).

Suggested public blurb (short):
"Redwood uses trusted third-party subprocessors (for storage, observability, and some GPU providers) to operate the Hosted API. We keep a current list of subprocessors and the regions where they process data; customers can review the list in the Console. For regulated data, we offer private deployment options and contractual safeguards like standard contractual clauses and additional audit rights."

Why: keeps it readable, mentions private option for regulated customers, doesn't attempt to enumerate legal mechanisms in detail.

Two legal flags: 1) avoid the phrasing "we keep a current list" unless we commit to a specific frequency of updates (recommend: "we maintain a publicly accessible list"); 2) the reference to "audit rights" needs qualification (we should say "customer-specific audit rights under certain enterprise contracts").

I left line edits in the doc. I'll run the DPA cross-check after lunch.

-Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Layperson summary for hosted API & console: subprocessors & cross-border transfers

Marcus —

Thanks for sending this through. A couple quick clarifying questions from Acme's procurement team before we share with our internal security reviewers:

1) Can you confirm whether the public subprocessor list will include the country of processing (not just vendor names)? Our security folks need that level of detail for initial risk triage.
2) In the FAQ you reference "standard contractual clauses" — will Redwood be providing a copy of the SCCs or a brief note that SCCs are used and where to find them?

We appreciate the plain-language approach; it makes our workflows much faster. If helpful, we can send suggested phrasing for procurement.

Best,
Aisha Gupta
Legal, Acme Corporation

Subject: Re: Layperson summary for hosted API & console: subprocessors & cross-border transfers

Aisha / Maria —

Quick answers to your procurement checks:
1) The public subprocessor list will include vendor name and primary processing region by country/continent. For example: "StorageCo — US, IE (backups processed in US)". We will not publish IP addresses or per-job telemetry.
2) We will provide a short note in the Console FAQ that SCCs are used for transfers from the EEA to other regions, and we'll link to a redacted copy of the SCCs and related transfer documentation. Enterprise customers can request full contractual language during negotiations.

Kim flagged two minor wording risks (see her inline suggestions). I tweaked the lead blurb to say "we maintain a publicly accessible list" and qualified "audit rights" to "customer-specific audit rights under certain enterprise contracts." Updated draft attached.

Next steps: Kim will confirm DPA alignment by EOD, Laura will confirm sales framing, and Vanessa/Stephanie will confirm Console placement constraints. If we can get internal sign-off today, I will share the short blurb with Acme and ask them for procurement feedback.

Marcus
Senior PM, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

This reads well and should cut the procurement back-and-forth. Two tiny edits that would help sales:
- Add one sentence in the Console copy: "If you need a tailored summary for your procurement packet, reach out to your Redwood account team." (helps route requests away from docs).
- In the FAQ, include a short line: "Where can I see the current subprocessor list? Console > Settings > Security" so reps can point customers to a location.

I reviewed the revised doc and I'm happy to sign off on the public blurb as long as Kim is OK on the DPA alignment.
